question: What does the CMOM approach for a sanitary sewer collection system mainly bring together?
correctAnswer: Capacity, management, operation and maintenance planning in one program
explanation: CMOM stands for capacity, management, operations and maintenance, and it joins those elements into one planned program for the collection system.
options: Only emergency repairs after overflows occur
Capacity, management, operation and maintenance planning in one program
Only the purchase of new cleaning equipment
Only the setting of sewer use rates
optionA: Only emergency repairs after overflows occur
optionB: Capacity, management, operation and maintenance planning in one program
optionC: Only the purchase of new cleaning equipment
optionD: Only the setting of sewer use rates

So older pipes can be removed from the records
So flow meters are no longer needed anywhere in the system

question: How does pipe bursting renew a buried sewer?

explanation: Pipe bursting breaks the old pipe outward into the soil while a new pipe is pulled in behind the bursting head.

A resin liner is cured inside the old pipe
The old pipe is washed and left in place as the new pipe
The old pipe is lifted out through the manholes intact
optionA: A bursting head fractures the old pipe and pushes the fragments into the surrounding soil while pulling a new pipe into the same alignment
optionB: A resin liner is cured inside the old pipe
optionC: The old pipe is washed and left in place as the new pipe
optionD: The old pipe is lifted out through the manholes intact

Slip lining always increases the pipe capacity
Pipe bursting requires no access pits in any situation

question: Two adjacent basins have similar size and age. Basin A has much higher night time minimum flows than Basin B during a dry, high groundwater period. What should the utility investigate first in Basin A?
correctAnswer: Sources of groundwater infiltration such as defective joints, cracked pipes and leaking manholes
explanation: High night minimum flows in dry weather with high groundwater point to infiltration sources that should be investigated first.
options: Sources of groundwater infiltration such as defective joints, cracked pipes and leaking manholes
Whether residents in Basin A take longer showers
The colour of the manhole covers in Basin A
The brand of flow monitor used in Basin B
optionA: Sources of groundwater infiltration such as defective joints, cracked pipes and leaking manholes
optionB: Whether residents in Basin A take longer showers
optionC: The colour of the manhole covers in Basin A
optionD: The brand of flow monitor used in Basin B
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

question: A flow monitoring study finds that measured dry weather flow in a basin is well above the flow estimated from water consumption records for the same area. What does the difference most likely represent?
correctAnswer: Extraneous water entering the sewer, mainly groundwater infiltration
explanation: Dry weather flow well above the water use estimate indicates extraneous water, mainly groundwater infiltration, entering the sewer.
options: Water lost through evaporation inside the sewer
Sewage that was treated twice at the plant
Errors in the customer water meters only
Extraneous water entering the sewer, mainly groundwater infiltration
optionA: Water lost through evaporation inside the sewer
optionB: Sewage that was treated twice at the plant
optionC: Errors in the customer water meters only
optionD: Extraneous water entering the sewer, mainly groundwater infiltration
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: What does rainfall dependent infiltration and inflow describe?
correctAnswer: The extra flow that enters a sanitary sewer in response to a storm, through defects, connections and saturated soil
explanation: RDII is the storm driven extra flow that reaches a sanitary sewer through defects, connections and saturated soil.
options: The normal dry weather flow from homes and businesses
The flow pumped by a lift station at the peak hour
The extra flow that enters a sanitary sewer in response to a storm, through defects, connections and saturated soil
The rain that runs off into a separate storm sewer only
optionA: The normal dry weather flow from homes and businesses
optionB: The flow pumped by a lift station at the peak hour
optionC: The extra flow that enters a sanitary sewer in response to a storm, through defects, connections and saturated soil
optionD: The rain that runs off into a separate storm sewer only
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

question: In an RDII analysis, the R value for a basin expresses which relationship?
correctAnswer: The share of rainfall volume over the tributary area that shows up as RDII flow in the sewer
explanation: The R value is the fraction of the rainfall volume over the basin that appears in the sewer as RDII.
options: The ratio of pipe length to manhole count
The share of rainfall volume over the tributary area that shows up as RDII flow in the sewer
The share of the budget spent on monitoring
The ratio of peak hour flow to average flow on dry days
optionA: The ratio of pipe length to manhole count
optionB: The share of rainfall volume over the tributary area that shows up as RDII flow in the sewer
optionC: The share of the budget spent on monitoring
optionD: The ratio of peak hour flow to average flow on dry days

question: A basin shows a fast, sharp RDII response that peaks during the storm and ends soon after. Which source is most consistent with that response shape?
correctAnswer: Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders, foundation drains or cross connections
explanation: A sharp response that tracks the storm matches direct inflow sources that connect quickly to the sewer.
options: Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders, foundation drains or cross connections
Slow groundwater infiltration through deep cracked pipes
Base sanitary flow from industrial dischargers
Flow released from upstream storage tanks
optionA: Direct inflow sources such as roof leaders, foundation drains or cross connections
optionB: Slow groundwater infiltration through deep cracked pipes
optionC: Base sanitary flow from industrial dischargers
optionD: Flow released from upstream storage tanks

question: After a lining program in one basin, RDII volume for similar storms drops by about half, while a nearby unlined basin shows no change. What is the best interpretation?
correctAnswer: The lining reduced rainfall dependent entry in the treated basin, and the comparison basin supports that the change came from the work
explanation: A drop in the treated basin with no change in a similar untreated basin supports that the lining reduced RDII.
options: Rainfall must have stopped reaching the treated basin
The flow monitors in the treated basin must all have failed
Lining increased RDII and the data should be discarded
The lining reduced rainfall dependent entry in the treated basin, and the comparison basin supports that the change came from the work
optionA: Rainfall must have stopped reaching the treated basin
optionB: The flow monitors in the treated basin must all have failed
optionC: Lining increased RDII and the data should be discarded
optionD: The lining reduced rainfall dependent entry in the treated basin, and the comparison basin supports that the change came from the work
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why do RDII hydrographs from the same basin often show a long, slow tail after the main peak has passed?
correctAnswer: Rain induced infiltration through saturated soil and defects keeps entering after direct inflow sources have stopped
explanation: The slow tail is rain induced infiltration that continues through saturated soil and defects after direct inflow ends.
options: The flow monitor continues recording after it is removed
Pumps at the plant push flow back into the basin
Rain induced infiltration through saturated soil and defects keeps entering after direct inflow sources have stopped
Residents delay all water use until after storms
optionA: The flow monitor continues recording after it is removed
optionB: Pumps at the plant push flow back into the basin
optionC: Rain induced infiltration through saturated soil and defects keeps entering after direct inflow sources have stopped
optionD: Residents delay all water use until after storms
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

question: A flow study measures an infiltration and inflow rate of 15 L/s from a tributary area of 50 ha. What is the I&I rate per hectare? Round to 1 decimal place.
correctAnswer: 0.3 L/s per ha
explanation: Rate = Q / A. Substitute the stated values: 15 ÷ 50 = 0.3 L/s per ha. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place(s). The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

question: For a storm, the RDII coefficient R is 0.04, rainfall is 25 mm, and the tributary area is 10 ha. Use 10 m³ of rainfall volume per mm per ha. What is the RDII volume? Round to 0 decimal places.
correctAnswer: 100 m³
explanation: V = R × P × A × 10. Substitute the stated values: 0.04 × 25 × 10 × 10 = 100 m³. Round only the final result to 0 decimal place(s). The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.

question: A flow meter at the outlet of a monitored basin records an average total flow of 50 L/s during a 4 hour wet weather event. The dry weather baseline flow for the same basin is 20 L/s. Use 3,600 seconds per hour and 1,000 L per m³. What volume of rainfall dependent infiltration and inflow entered the system during the event? Round to 0 decimal places.
correctAnswer: 432 m³
explanation: V = (Qwet - Qdry) × t × 3600/1000. Substitute the stated values: (50 - 20) × 4 × 3600 ÷ 1000 = 432 m³. Round only the final result to 0 decimal place(s). The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.
